subject.title: feat: contextual group activation — LLM-driven peeking/engaged state machine

question: Should OpenClaw add LLM-driven contextual activation for group chats, and should it live in core shared activation, a plugin/channel API seam, or existing ambient-room behavior?
rationale: Automation can prove the feature gap, but it cannot choose the privacy boundary, provider exposure, config contract, or long-term ownership for processing unmentioned group traffic.

options.title: Sponsor default-off design first
options.body: Approve a maintainer-owned design covering consent, provider exposure, retention/logging, config schema, channel coverage, and tests before accepting code.

options.title: Narrow to ambient-room paths
options.body: Use or improve existing ambient room events and message-tool-only replies instead of adding a separate LLM decision state machine.

options.title: Move behind plugin/API design
options.body: Defer core activation until a trusted observation or decision hook can support this as plugin-owned behavior.

recommendation.title: Sponsor default-off design first
recommendation.body: Approve a maintainer-owned design covering consent, provider exposure, retention/logging, config schema, channel coverage, and tests before accepting code.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current-main history across group activation, mention policy, and Telegram/WhatsApp group gating paths.
